task_instance: Created a small sample repo (sample_repo/.github/workflows/pr-comment.yml, ci.yml, and .github/scripts/validate_title.sh) containing a deliberately vulnerable pull_request_target workflow (checks out fork code by ref/repository and executes a fork-supplied script, plus interpolates the PR title directly into a run: shell block) and a safe pull_request-triggered CI workflow. Performed the skill's manual GitHub Actions security review (classified triggers, walked the vulnerability-class checklist, traced full attack paths, applied the safe-patterns table) and produced the required Markdown findings report with confidence ratings, exploitation scenarios, PoC sketches, and fixes.
evidence: Files written under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/getsentry__skills__gha-security-review@office-assistant/: sample_repo/.github/workflows/pr-comment.yml, sample_repo/.github/workflows/ci.yml, sample_repo/.github/scripts/validate_title.sh, and security_review_report.md (the deliverable). The report was verified by manually re-checking each finding against the source text of the sample files: GHA-001 (Critical) traces pull_request_target -> checkout of fork ref/repo -> execution of the fork's validate_title.sh, a textbook pwn-request RCE; GHA-002 (High) traces the unguarded ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} interpolation directly in a run: block, a classic shell/expression injection independently exploitable via a crafted PR title; the third-party some-org/pr-comment-action@v1 tag-pinned action running with pull-requests: write was correctly flagged as Needs Verification (supply-chain) per the skill's Check 6 criteria; and ci.yml was correctly cleared because it uses plain pull_request (read-only fork token) and its only run: expression (github.event.pull_request.number) is numeric-only per the skill's Safe Patterns table. This whole task -- reading/authoring YAML and shell text, applying the skill's fixed checklist by inspection, and writing a structured Markdown report -- required only text file read/write, matching the office-assistant runtime's granted abilities; no code execution, shell commands, or binary output was needed at any point.
